name: Dictators of the Twentieth Century
description: Strongmen and one-party rulers who held absolute power across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, and the wars and fall of their regimes.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and fascism
checkpoints.note: Lenin founds the Soviet state, Stalin takes it over, Mussolini invents fascism in Italy and Hitler takes power in Germany.

checkpoints.name: War and its aftermath
checkpoints.note: Hitler and Mussolini drag Europe deeper into war, Franco, who won Spain's civil war in 1939, keeps his country out of it, and Chiang fights Japan. The war ends in Allied victory in 1945, and Stalin dies in 1953.

checkpoints.name: Cold War strongmen
checkpoints.note: Mao, Tito, Kim Il Sung, Peron and Salazar rule in the shadow of the superpowers. Pinochet, Suharto and Idi Amin take power by force, Marcos rules the Philippines under martial law, and Pol Pot's Khmer Rouge rule Cambodia until Vietnam drives them out in 1979.

checkpoints.name: The last regimes
checkpoints.note: Communist rulers fall in Eastern Europe in 1989 and Ceausescu is executed, Mobutu is ousted in 1997, and Khomeini, Saddam Hussein and Gaddafi mark the final years of the century and after.
